title: Science Without Scientists?
gist: Sami Mahroum argues that as autonomous AI systems generate hypotheses, design experiments and write up results, scientific knowledge needs sources that are trusted and publicly answerable, since credibility rests on social trust. Excerpt only.

insights.claim: Autonomous systems can now generate their own hypotheses, design experiments and write up results, forcing the scientific community to adapt.
insights.speaker: @MahroumS
insights.so_what: AI-run research shifts value toward validation and accountability layers.

insights.claim: For scientific knowledge to retain its standing, its sources must be trusted and answerable to the public.
insights.speaker: @MahroumS
insights.so_what: Validation and audit mechanisms become a prerequisite for AI-generated science to be accepted.

insights.claim: Most scientific claims are received without any means of checking them, so people judge the credibility of whoever stands behind the claim rather than the claim itself.
insights.speaker: @MahroumS
insights.so_what: Explains why AI authorship can undermine acceptance even of correct findings.
insights.quote: we tend to judge not the claim but the credibility of whoever stands behind it

insights.claim: Harvard historian of science Steven Shapin shows that producing scientific truth has long been inseparable from the social work of persuading one's peers.
insights.speaker: @MahroumS
insights.so_what: Frames science as a social-trust system, not only a fact-generation process.
